# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54. The site is a small Nuxt app. Its pages are built in the browser, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript may see an empty page. The Trail guides page is also marked noindex. The one unknown is the canonical link, which depends on which domain you want to use. No blocker applied, so there is no cap. These results are read from code. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Send real page content from the server (GEO-003) - **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends and don't run JavaScript, so they may see an empty page. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small. Turn on server rendering, or prerender the routes. - **Score after this:** 59–67 ### 2. Make the sitemap link in robots.txt an absolute URL (GEO-011) - **Why it matters:** the `Sitemap:` line must be a full URL for crawlers to find your page list reliably. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4` - **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 54–63 ### 3. Link to Trail guides with a real link (GEO-016) - **Why it matters:** crawlers follow `` links. The only route from the home page to `/guides` is a button click handled by script. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Use ``. - **Score after this:** 54–63 Next in line: remove the noindex on `/guides` (GEO-014, about +1.5 points) and give each page its own title and description (GEO-012, +2 points). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is readable and valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, a small plain-text file with valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can reach the site | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2`, only `/admin` is blocked. I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json`. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`. 1 of 2 sampled routes is clear (`/` is clear, `/guides` is noindex). | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical link | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical anywhere, and no declared domain. `trailhead.example` appears only in the sitemap. | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2`, site-wide | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is linked | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4`, the `Sitemap:` line is relative. `public/sitemap.xml` itself is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2`. Every page shares one title and description. `lang` is set in `nuxt.config.ts:5`. | | GEO-016 | Pages reachable by normal links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`, `/guides` has no `` link | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` sets only `noindex`, not `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | I read `app.vue` and the three pages. There are no images, the button has text, and a title is set. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. It's optional and not scored. | ## Other problems found None found beyond the scored results above. ## Worth considering - **The Trail guides page promises routes but lists none:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. Listing the routes with their grades as text, ideally each on its own page, would give readers and machines something to quote. - **The home page says little about the site:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. A short intro of what the site covers, as text, might help. - **Admin is blocked from crawlers and also marked noindex:** `public/robots.txt:2`: `Disallow: /admin`, and `pages/admin.vue:2`: `name: 'robots', content: 'noindex'`. Crawlers blocked by `robots.txt` can't see the noindex. Keep one of the two, or leave it as is if the block is what you want. - **No canonical link or site URL is configured:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://trailhead.example/`. Declare your real domain and add an absolute canonical per page. - **The noindex on `/guides` conflicts with the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `/guides`, but `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` sets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on it. If that's deliberate, remove it from the sitemap. If not, remove the header. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015:** no domain is declared, so I can't judge canonicals. Tell me your real domain. - **GEO-003:** a hosting layer could prerender the pages, which code can't show. A live check would settle it. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. - `/admin` is meant to stay private, so I left it out of the sampled routes. - Sampled routes were `/` and `/guides`. That is every public route in the repository. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
